chunks: My father - may God be pleased with him - narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Attar narrated to us, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad, from Abu Sa'id al-Adamy, from Abdul Aziz al-Abdi, from Ibn Abi Ya'foor, who said: I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) say:
Whoever attaches his heart to the world, it attaches to him from it with three characteristics: a grief that does not perish, an aspiration that is not attained, and a hope that is not achieved.

key_terms.الدُّنْيَا: The world, worldly life, or temporal existence

ai.seo_question: What are the three characteristics that result from attaching the heart to the world according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: In *Al-Khisal*, Shaykh al-Saduq presents this hadith as a causal chain where a single spiritual defect—attachment to the world—generates three specific psychological afflictions. This triad of *hamm* (endless worry), *amal* (vain hope), and *raja'* (unfulfilled expectation) illustrates the Shia concept of how materialism disrupts inner peace, contrasting the fleeting nature of dunya with the enduring state of the soul.

en.dr-ali-peiravi: 3-22 (The compiler of the book narrated) that his father - may God be pleased with him - narrated that Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Attar quoted Muhammad ibn Ahmad, on the authority of Abi Sa’id al-Adamy, on the authority of Abdul Aziz al-Abdi that Ibn Abi Ya’foor said, “I heard Aba Abdullah as-Sadiq (MGB) say, ‘
Whoever gets attached to this world has only grabbed onto continual grief, unattainable aspirations and unreachable hopes.’”
